Definition: (including the other inflections); from G5104 and G3778; truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality):--like, such (an one).
BiblicalUsage: Of this sort — the word measures a thing by its kind. Paul says such fornication as is reported among the Corinthians is not so much as named among the Gentiles, and he says of the disciplined man that sufficient to such a man is the punishment inflicted of many.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mirror is held up to the church here: the sin is named by its sort, and the punishment is measured by the same sort.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
